title: Paired cuda5 comparison of the range-split scorer with the existing baselines
question: With all implementations timed on the same GPU in one session, how does the range-split scorer's batch-1 latency compare with adapted GPUSparse monolithic, CSR full-byte B16/B32 and the CSR exhaustive control?
hypothesis: Identical canonical top-10 for all five; latency ratios are empirical.
motivation: Turn the 2026-11-13 exploratory, unpaired comparison into a paired one under the 2026-11-12 protocol.

declared_changes.vs_2026_11_13: baselines now run in the same session; no scorer change
declared_changes.vs_2026_11_12: adds range-bitpack and a CSR exhaustive B32 control; monolithic fixtures at PL512 only; local gate stand-in instead of the team runner; new bootstrap seed 20261114

correctness_rule: zero canonical mismatches for every implementation against the CPU oracle; any failure stops before timing
success_rule: All correctness passes and the 15 timing processes complete.
failure_rule: A correctness failure is reported and stops the run; higher latency is a valid negative result.
next_if_negative: Kernel-time breakdown of the range scorer; decide between layout changes and range pruning.
recording_ids: not recorded by the team runtime
